Read NONMEM table output

Source: R/tables.R
pmx_read_tables.Rd

Reads the files a NONMEM $TABLE record writes, to compare a translation against the run's own predictions with pmx_compare(tables, model). The comparison simulates the model on the table's records, so the table needs the dosing records as well as the observations.

Usage

pmx_read_tables(file, prediction = "PRED")

Arguments

file

The path of a table file, or several from one run.

prediction

The name of the prediction column.

Value

A zufapmx_tables object: a list with records, a data frame with columns id, time, evid, amt, cmt, rate, ii, addl, ss and pred followed by the table's other columns under their own names; prediction, the column read as pred; digits, the significant digits of the prediction column; and files.

Details

A table is NONMEM's layout: an optional TABLE NO. n title line, a line of column names, then one record per line, separated by spaces or commas. Several files from one run (say sdtab1 and patab1) are read side by side: they must have the same records, and a column in more than one file must hold the same values in each.

The records need ID, TIME and the prediction column. AMT, EVID, MDV, CMT, RATE, II, ADDL and SS are read when present, with NONMEM's defaults when not. Without EVID, a record with a positive AMT is a dose and any other record with MDV 0 (or no MDV) is an observation. Records that are neither are dropped, and EVID 3 and 4 (resets) are refused. Every other column is kept, so the model's covariates can come from the table. Column names match without regard to case.

The prediction column should be PRED, NONMEM's population prediction: the comparison simulates the model's typical subject, every random effect at zero (design Q1). NONMEM prints a fixed number of significant digits, 5 by default; the reader records it, and the comparison accepts a prediction that rounds to the table's value.

Tables are read with the zucsv package when it is installed, and with base R otherwise; both give the same result.

See also

pmx_compare() compares a model with the tables.

Other readers: pmx_read_mrgsolve(), pmx_read_nonmem(), pmx_read_rxode2(), pmx_write_json()

Examples

file <- tempfile(fileext = ".tab")
writeLines(c(
  "TABLE NO.  1",
  " ID          TIME        AMT         EVID        PRED",
  "  1.0000E+00  0.0000E+00  1.0000E+02  1.0000E+00  0.0000E+00",
  "  1.0000E+00  1.0000E+00  0.0000E+00  0.0000E+00  1.8187E+00"
), file)
pmx_read_tables(file)
#> <zufapmx tables> 1 subject, 1 dose and 1 observation records
#> Prediction: `PRED`, 5 significant digits.
#> From file194e3ef2450b.tab.
